$comment: Client ↔ hub API breaks accepted on purpose, checked by `pnpm check:api-compat` (scripts/check-api-compat.mjs) against the latest release. Key = the break as the check prints it; value = why it is fine (the client tolerates it, the feature is gated with hubHasFeature, …). oldClient = the release's app on this hub; newClient = this app on the release's hub. `--prune` drops entries nothing needs.

oldClient.sharing.sharedWithMe removed: Removed on purpose (abd614975: guest sharing reversed). A v0.43 app’s sidebar SharedWithMe renders null when the query has no data, so on a newer hub the section just stays hidden.
oldClient.app.backup.create output: BackupInfo.type gained 'restore' (the pre-restore copy). An older app's Settings shows the type as a label; an unknown value only loses its badge colour.
oldClient.app.backup.list output: Same as app.backup.create: BackupInfo.type gained 'restore'; an older app renders it as plain text.
oldClient.app.backup.restore output: Was void, now a RestoreResult; an older app ignores the value. NOT seamless: a v0.44 app connected to a server hub could not restore before (the hub refused), and now can; afterwards it does not reload (it has no dataGeneration watcher) and keeps showing the old data until the user reloads it. Accepted: it cannot be told apart from a current client (both send clientApi 1), admin-only, and it leaves data correct on the hub.

newClient.app.backup.restoreStatus added: Gated: Settings calls it only when the hub has the 'hub-restart-restore' feature (hubHasFeature).
newClient.app.backup.restore output: Gated: Settings reads the RestoreResult only when the hub has 'hub-restart-restore'; an older hub answers nothing and relaunches the app as before.
newClient.hub.describe output: dataGeneration added. The client reads it as unknown (transport hubDataGeneration.ts): a hub older than the field sends none, and the window simply never reloads for it.
